surface_verification.justification: jsdom has no layout engine, so none of the 4 reported bugs (form/panel too tall, panel clipped left, excessive card spacing, uncollapsible filter bar) can be proven by unit tests alone — real bounding-box geometry, real flex-height allocation, and a real max-md: media-query breakpoint all require a real browser. This suite (client/e2e/flows/mobile-triage-form-layout.spec.ts + mobile-triage-spacing-filters.spec.ts, split to clear the 300-line bloat gate) runs all 4 ACs at 375×667 (and desktop, for AC3/AC4's unchanged-above-breakpoint half) via client/e2e/isolated-stack.mjs against a real Chromium. All 8 pass; case 3 of AC1 (a deliberately forced-overflow stress test) caught a genuine, previously-shipped production bug during development (ModalShell.tsx's body-slot wrapper needed flex flex-col, not just min-h-0 flex-1, for max-h-full to resolve) — disclosed in full in the iterate spec's Confidence Calibration, along with the one honestly-disclosed gap: the original bug report's vh-vs-dvh mechanism is structurally unreproducible in headless Chromium (no real, resizable browser chrome), verified via git-stash falsification.
